newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua asks OAS mission to stay.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua asks OAS mission to stay.

text.p: Worried by popular unrest over delays in the general election vote count, the Nicaraguan government on Wednesday asked the Organisation of American States (OAS) observer mission to stay until it was completed.

Ten days after Nicaragua's general elections, authorities still have not announced the winners, and post-election tensions are rising amid charges of election irregularities and wild, self-proclaimed victory celebrations.

Nicaragua's Supreme Election Council (CSE) has said it will announce the official winners in mid-November after it reviews the vote count at the request of various parties who alleged it was riddled with anomalies.
President Violeta Chamorro and the Catholic Church have urged the CSE to hurry the count to stave off potential instability and the police have banned public demonstrations.

In a letter to OAS chief Cesar Gaviria, Nicaraguan Foreign Minister Ernesto Leal said "the continued presence of the electoral observation mission would strengthen Nicaragua's nascent democracy and support the transparence and legitimacy of the election process."
In the presidential race, right-winger Arnoldo Aleman of the Liberal Alliance has a 49 to 38 percent lead over his left-wing Sandinista rival Daniel Ortega in the preliminary vote count.
But Ortega has refused to concede defeat, saying he will wait until the official announcement, hinting darkly at election fraud by his right-wing rivals.
